note: Ireland issues no national identity card. The Public Services Card the Minister for Social Protection issues (Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005, s. 263) is for transactions with the bodies the Act specifies: anyone else who seeks to have it produced commits an offence, so it isn't an identity card the holder shows at large.

sources.title: Law Reform Commission, Revised Acts, Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005, section 263, Public services card
sources.said: The Minister may F1560 [ , subject to subsection (1C) , ] issue a card (in this Act referred to as a ‘ public services card ’ ) to a person in such form as the Minister considers fit for the purposes of carrying out a transaction. ... (4) A person who uses or attempts to use a F1558 [ public services card ] or seeks to have a F1558 [ public services card ] produced to him or her, other than— ( a ) the person who is the holder of the card or a person appointed to act on behalf of the cardholder, ( b ) a specified body, for the purposes of a transaction,
